facts.statement: The genus Torvoneustes was described by Andrade and colleagues in 2010.
The type species for the genus Torvoneustes is Dakosaurus carpenteri.
The species T. carpenteri was previously known as Dakosaurus carpenteri and Geosaurus carpenteri.
facts.quote: synonyms: Dakosaurus carpenteri Wilkinson et al., 2008 Geosaurus carpenteri Young & Andrade, 2009

facts.statement: Torvoneustes is unique among its relatives for having a false-ziphodont dentition.
facts.quote: Torvoneustes is unique in having a false-ziphodont dentition.

facts.statement: T. carpenteri reached 4 to 4.7 meters in length, with some specimens suggesting an even larger size.
facts.quote: T. coryphaeus reached 3.7 m in length, while T. carpenteri reached 4 - 4.7 m in length; some specimens indicate an even larger body size.

facts.statement: The species T. jurensis was estimated to reach a length of 4 meters.
facts.quote: T. jurensis was estimated to have reached a length of 4 m.

facts.statement: The species T. carpenteri was named in honor of Simon Carpenter, an amateur geologist who discovered the fossils.
facts.quote: The species was named to honour Simon Carpenter, an amateur geologist from Frome in Somerset, who discovered the fossils.

facts.statement: Torvoneustes belongs to the subfamily Geosaurinae.
Torvoneustes is a member of the family Metriorhynchidae.
Torvoneustes lived from the Oxfordian to the Valanginian stages, between 159 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Valanginian (159 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Torvoneustes descended from a ziphodont ancestor or if Dakosaurus and Geosaurus evolved their dentition independently.
facts.quote: However, it is also possible that Dakosaurus and Geosaurus acquired similar dentitions independently, and that Torvoneustes is not descended from a ziphodont ancestor.

rejected.statement: Torvoneustes is an extinct genus of metriorhynchid thalattosuchian.
rejected.quote: Torvoneustes is an extinct genus of metriorhynchid thalattosuchian.
